answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns (four seasons of three ordinary rounds); courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: each player takes twelve ordinary turns; courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters (each one space); resolve round event; resolve monument/Servants’ Hall ongoing effects; choose an activity; invite exactly its required gentry; provide all required services; resolve positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one tile; cleanup used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Hosting steps 1–8 and Player Reference: Host.

answers.answer: Passing order: servants directly to Available; gentry in discard to hand; round-track event, then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free full Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances marker. Servants used for ongoing effects go to Expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → event/ongoing effects → choose £200 or free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.

answers.answer: Yes. Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2, so 6.1 qualifies the PR6 activity and guests even if four Service Help actions reduce current reputation to 3.4 afterward. Each Service Help costs three increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2… remains the screening level for the whole activity. Service Help moves one servant from Quarters to Available.

answers.answer: Resolve every positive favour before every negative favour. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss; the summary says resolve positives first and losses stop at 1.1. A guest with a money penalty requires paying it in full; positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money may fund it. If short, borrow if possible; if still unable to pay, you cannot play the guest.
answers.evidence: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours… A money penalty must be fully payable… If money is short, you must borrow if possible.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one Quarters servant to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments, fully refresh; once per turn. At minimum 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table; at minimum you… cannot take a special action. Service Help… cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry; take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, except underbutlers, into Expended Service, with no hiring fee. On its first use it upgrades. The upgraded room may instead recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Room: … no gentry. Take up to two servants… into Expended Service… upgraded room alternatively lets you recruit one common servant… from any location on one opponent’s family board.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler can substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even when that type is available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: housekeeper… only when no lady’s maids are available; Brushing Room footman substitution… no valets; underbutler… even when that type remains available.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it goes immediately from supply to Expended Service. It normally moves to Quarters at your next rotation and to Available at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service can make it available earlier, and Quarters effects can help once it is there. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry is the only way… take one… into Expended Service… second subsequent rotation… opponent can never recruit your underbutler.

answers.answer: Market cost is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus modifier. Minimum price is £100. You may not acquire a duplicate of a tile you own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing tiles above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300… cannot fall below £100… Never acquire a duplicate… otherwise reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and you draw again; duplicates share one space and its price. Reserve-eligible tiles go directly to Reserve and you draw again. When filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves the space occupied and causes no refill.
answers.evidence: Refill: if a Market space became empty, slide remaining tiles left… duplicate… stack… draw again… Qualifying Reserve tiles go straight to Reserve…

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; subsequent Service draws also go there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; subsequent PR1 draws go there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve… after courtship 1… Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar… after courtship 2… PR1 tiles… Full refresh occurs after each of the first three courtships.

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships 1–3, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Score the current face-up theme, including negative tile VP; only the currently face-up hybrid category counts. Highest wins one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied, each tied player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Each player discards one secret objective; shuffle discards together and bottom-deck them. Then move Reserve tiles, refresh Market, reveal the next theme, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance round marker.
answers.evidence: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds… In courtships 1–3… If tied… After courtships 1–3… pass first-player marker anticlockwise.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores tile VP for all four revealed themes, with repeated categories counted repeatedly including negative VP. Highest receives a VP card and Fairchild; ties break on reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild and tied players draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players may use special actions and VP-card benefits where possible before moving to Wedding Bells and scoring. The summary does not specify any further last-action categories beyond these.
answers.evidence: Final courtship… total tile VP for all four revealed theme cards… Then players have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for their benefits where possible.

answers.answer: VP categories: improvement tiles (all face-up printed VP, including negatives and unused); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded); fulfilled objectives; reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; servants score 2 each; wealth scores 1 per £200 rounded down; retained VP cards score printed VP. Victory ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise higher reputation level; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie rule.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup plus two on round 6, then discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or VP cards increase retained final objectives and do not cause an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together before being put face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tile at game end; it need not be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Normally receive five at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three… shuffle simultaneous discards together… not upgrading them.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it for its benefit; used VP cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards remain hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; a card cannot provide both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: A VP card offers a choice… immediately on drawing… later turn… once more after final courtship… Used VP cards go to the bottom… retained ones stay hidden.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side at cleanup after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile remains upgraded. Hybrids start with the underlined icon and flip after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. Tiles that upgrade into ongoing monuments have one activity use, upgrade into the monument, and cannot host again. Only a hybrid’s currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Normal activity tiles must upgrade after first use… Hybrids… flip after every use… Only that face-up category counts for courtship and objectives. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite… can never host again.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve during the ongoing-effects step after the round event, on hosting and passing turns; monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn, not during courtship. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant to reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; that servant cannot also serve the activity and goes to Expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments… per ordinary turn… hosting or passing. Servants’ Hall… place any one available servant… Do not target a player at minimum reputation.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile, one casual guest from hand plus normal guest service; doubles all favours including negative; remains an upgraded activity. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand plus normal service; doubles one chosen favour, others normal; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest to attend, no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours and excludes negative favours from doubling; retain guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table; all three suites have a fixed count of one guest.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player and give them the first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Bonuses: Asquith adds Dowager Countess as fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts at reputation level 1, position 1 (Cavendish instead starts 1.4); counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, and Max are stacked with 1 showing and Max bottom, with 7/8 counters unused. Starting Available Service: one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, footman. Five tiles: Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green. Family cards: Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady; Asquith also Dowager Countess. Ponsonby is the family that starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are included. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Stock one valet and one lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants… unavailable this game.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle starters and deal two to each player; shuffle every unused starter back into casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules, not a separate play guest type.
answers.evidence: Setup: separate starter guests… deal two… shuffle every unused starter back… Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon.

answers.answer: For four players select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). At most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze may be selected. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments are always in the bag and do not count against this selection.
answers.evidence: Select one double-sided monument per player plus one, choosing at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze… tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count.

answers.answer: Opening Market has six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including none), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside then return them after filling. Stack duplicate eligible tiles in one space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort six spaces by ascending sorting number starting at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Set Alderley Hall standard side up with round marker at 1 and one reminder token per player above track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme and keep revealed themes in order; put base Charles and Elizabeth face up on Alderley Hall. First theme is open, not hidden, and old themes remain in order rather than leaving play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9: reveal the first theme (open courtship); keep revealed themes in order through the game.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available; the servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each advances one space only. An unused servant already in Available remains there.
answers.evidence: Rotate service: move servants in Servants’ Quarters to Available first, then those in Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters… Unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No immediate Fair reward if the Study is not upgraded at the event step; hosting and upgrading it later that turn does not earn the missed reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Village Fair: if your Private Study is already upgraded, immediately gain £300 and 2 reputation. No reward if it is not upgraded at this step.

answers.answer: Round 6 event is resolved before ongoing tile effects, on each player’s turn whether hosting or passing. Draw two objectives and keep both secret with other objectives; passing players receive the event too.
answers.evidence: Round-track events resolved before ongoing effects; space 6 Draw Objectives: draw two objectives; keep both secret. Passing events use same position/order.

answers.answer: Yes. On National Holiday (space 14), ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements, including service and exact gentry counts and types, remain in force.
answers.evidence: National Holiday: Ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting; still obey all other requirements, including service and gentry counts/types.

answers.answer: Yes, Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds at prices applicable before buying starts. Finish all purchases in the unchanged market before sliding/refilling; no refresh between purchases. Reserve may be used. Market Purchase VP cards use the same multiple-purchase and no-refresh rules; resulting empty Market spaces refill together afterward.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card: buy any number… finish all purchases before sliding/refilling… single unchanged market… restriction applies to both.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside; leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six Market spaces from the bag under normal refill rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Removed tiles cannot reappear during that refresh. Reserve tiles are unaffected.
answers.evidence: Refresh: set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged… then return set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. They cannot reappear in same refresh.

answers.answer: Reputation symbols are increments. Moving from position 5 to 1 increases level; from 1 to 5 decreases level. Each full level spans five increments. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions (which can be taken before or mid-favour to make room).
answers.evidence: Reputation symbols are one increment… crossing boundaries… minimum 1.1, maximum 7.5… Ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately.

answers.answer: Money held is public, and players may not give or receive money between each other. Never spend more than you have. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Money held is public… may not give or receive money between players… never spend more… Money supply is unlimited.

answers.answer: Two ladies may include female family members or female guests. Two casual guests must be casual guests and cannot be family. Extra or fewer gentry than the exact printed requirement are not allowed. Family requires no personal service and has no PR; guests and activity tile must meet reputation screening, except where PR is waived (e.g. National Holiday).
answers.evidence: Ladies includes every female family member or female guest… casual requirements require that guest type and exclude family… cannot exceed or fall short… family… no PR and no personal service.

answers.answer: An ordinary invite-guest favour draws one card from the indicated deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to hand; explicit larger counts apply. Screening draws the stated number, chooses the stated number to keep, reveals only kept cards, and adds them to hand. Rejected cards go unrevealed to the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Invite Guest favour… draw a new card… reveal… add to hand. For screening… reveal only kept cards… rejected cards on bottom… without revealing.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so with no unwanted guests you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including a guest drawn earlier in Enjoy Favours; family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Dismissal is always optional… choose eligible guest from hand, current activity or discard… can be guest just drawn… family can never be dismissed… no longer yours.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Young Lady: draw one casual guest. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits. The Young Lady’s admirer bonus is separate and conditional on a male prestige guest attending.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table.

answers.answer: The admirer bonus applies only when a male prestige guest attends with the Young Lady, including the female attendee plus male prestige pairing; it gives two reputation. A male casual guest and Charles Fairchild do not qualify (Charles is prestige but the bonus says male prestige; Charles is male and is a prestige guest, so he does qualify). A female prestige guest does not qualify. She still draws one casual guest in all cases.
answers.evidence: Young Lady: Draw one casual guest; additionally gain two reputation if a male prestige guest attends the same activity. Charles is male and both Fairchilds are prestige guests.

answers.answer: Charles is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither has family dismissal immunity; they are guests and may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Charles Fairchild is male and Elizabeth female… both prestige guests with no PR; Charles requires valet, Elizabeth lady’s maid… Charles gives three reputation. Elizabeth gives both… Neither Fairchild has family dismissal immunity.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes the player lose one reputation. Opponents at minimum reputation cannot be targeted by reputation-reducing effects.
answers.evidence: Base gossips… Perkins (reduce one opponent by one)… Florence… reduce one opponent by two, and lose one yourself; minimum-reputation protection still applies.

answers.answer: Barn earns one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives none.
answers.evidence: Barn: every time you host an Estate activity, gain one reputation. It gives no reputation just for owning an Estate tile or passing.

answers.answer: Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant still in Quarters after ordinary rotation, in addition to Available Service, without reputation cost; send it to Expended at turn end. Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended to Quarters. Service Help instead costs 3 increments per servant and moves one Quarters servant to Available (not directly from Expended).
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile: each turn… directly use one servant… after rotation… used servant goes to Expended. Service mechanism table.

answers.answer: Front-side Private Study requires two family and a butler, with no tile favour. On first use it upgrades permanently to an ongoing tile. It cannot be hosted repeatedly to obtain Village Fair income; upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation only when the Village Fair event occurs, without staffing/hosting.
answers.evidence: Private Study hosts two family with a butler… upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile… gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds only, without staffing or hosting it again.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the retained final objective count; they do not trigger extra discards.
answers.evidence: Main Library: unupgraded… butler and two family… one extra objective; upgraded… butler and three family… one VP card. Extra objectives increase… final objective total.

answers.answer: Objective VP benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. The kept objective adds one to final retained objective count.
answers.evidence: Objective VP card: draw two objectives, keep one, return the other to bottom… gives one additional retained objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended, and is usable immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Refresh Service… all servants directly to Available Service, including… Expended… Service Help… one… only from Quarters.

answers.answer: Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It does not immediately provide service from there; it must first progress through service movement, unless another applicable rule/effect enables use.
answers.evidence: Hire Servant: take one servant from Servants for Hire, not underbutler, into Expended Service; ordinary rotation advances servants one space.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return one gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, it may be selected to attend that activity subject to normal requirements; returning it does not automatically play it.
answers.evidence: Refresh Guest… including a family member from personal discard to hand… if returned before Invite Gentry… may choose that returned card to attend.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary servant scoring is 2 VP per servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids… Ordinary service VP counts all servants; 7 VP for at least ten servants total.

answers.answer: Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments after upgrading. For category objectives, a tile counts in its currently face-up category; a hybrid contributes only its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Monuments objective includes upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category bonus counts monuments and hybrids currently in that category; only face-up hybrid category counts.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Tiles need only be owned at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Nature Group — 11 VP… Domestic Group — 12 VP… Owning tiles at game end suffices; using or upgrading is unnecessary.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective gives 1 VP per prestige guest; every-three-guests objective gives 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests, with incomplete groups scoring zero. A final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest and is nonfamily, so it counts for both applicable objectives.
answers.evidence: Guest bonuses… per prestige guest; or 1 VP per complete three guests (all nonfamily guests)… prestige guests include a final Fairchild.

answers.answer: The reputation objective awards 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. Wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on level only (1/3/6/10/15/21/28 for levels 1–7); wheel position does not affect ordinary VP or reputation tie resolution.
answers.evidence: Reputation objective… maximum level (7), regardless of wheel position; wealth… at least £1200; reputation scoring and tie rule use level, not wheel position.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded favour draws one prestige guest. Upgraded favour draws one prestige guest and optionally dismisses one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of the appropriate decks. It remains an activity on both sides; it does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Base West Terrace remains an activity… both sides… one butler and exactly three family… upgraded… draw one prestige guest AND optionally dismiss one to four… never ongoing.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal discard pile limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally; guests remain yours until dismissed.
answers.evidence: There is no hand or discard-pile limit… discard-pile gentry score normally. Guests remain yours until dismissed.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Every Reserve tile is public… may inspect all tiles… buy any one… including a tile underneath another in a stack.

answers.answer: No. You may pass even if you could legally host. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Choose host an activity or pass… Without all required gentry and service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you may use the free Market refresh, also pay for one Refresh Market special action, and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each causing a separate full refresh. Only the special-action Refresh Market is limited to once per turn; pass and VP-card refreshes do not use that allowance. Purchase timing restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: Other refresh methods (pass benefit and VP cards) do not use up the once-per-turn special refresh allowance. Multiple Market Refresh VP cards… combine… one free passing-benefit refresh and one paid special-action refresh.
